title: Trump asserts U.S. has "total control" of Strait of Hormuz; Iran disputes claim
dek: President Trump stated on Truth Social that the U.S. has "total control" over the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Basij paramilitary unit head countered that the waterway is "under Iran's control and management." The competing claims highlight contested authority over a critical global shipping chokepoint during ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict.
author: The GoCheckMyNews Desk
key_fact: Trump wrote on Truth Social that the U.S. has "total control" of the Strait of Hormuz, while Iran's Basij chief asserted Iran controls and manages the waterway.
bottom_line: Trump's assertion and Iran's counterclaim represent rhetorical escalation during active conflict over a chokepoint vital to global energy supply. Watch for statements from other maritime powers, shipping insurers, or the U.S. Navy clarifying operational reality versus political assertion.
body: President Trump stated on his Truth Social platform that the U.S. has "total control" over the Strait of Hormuz, writing "I THINK WE WILL KEEP IT," according to CBS News reporting.

The assertion drew an immediate counterclaim from Iran's Basij paramilitary unit head Hossein Taeb, who asserted that the Strait of Hormuz is "under Iran's control and management," per CBS News reporting citing Reuters and Iran's semi-official Fars news agency. Iran's Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei added that "every party that benefits from commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz carries both a legal and a moral obligation to remediate the environmental harm," language that implies Iran's role in stewarding the waterway.

The competing claims emerged as the U.S.-Iran war approaches the six-month mark, according to CBS News. The Strait of Hormuz is the world's most critical oil transit route, and assertions of control over it carry material weight for global energy markets and shipping security.

The sourced reporting does not include specific military or operational actions underpinning Trump's claim, the current operational status of international shipping through the strait, comparative analysis of U.S. Navy presence versus Trump's assertion, or independent verification of either side's control claims beyond their on-record statements. Those details remain open questions.
